details: This package is a controlled ingestion-baseline / proof-of-concept record rather than malware. It ships package/backend-canary.js, which reads /etc/hostname and the OS username, SHA-256 hashes both values, and issues an HTTPS GET to a webhook[.]site callback with the hashes in host= and user= query parameters. Only those two hashed host-metadata values are transmitted; no credentials, tokens, environment values, file contents or wallet data are collected. package.json declares no lifecycle scripts and index.js only exports a constant, so the beacon runs only when backend-canary.js is executed directly, not on install or require. This package is a self-declared controlled baseline / canary artifact (package.json description "controlled npm backend ingestion baseline", marker file NPM_BACKEND_BASELINE_d6f5c69af448a09f64127a69cfd27b1f, index.js exporting the string 'controlled'). On load it performs a single host-metadata beacon: package/backend-canary.js computes SHA-256 over the contents of /etc/hostname and over the current username, then issues an HTTPS GET to hxxps://webhook[.]site/4f41cd5b-d1e6-4d37-8c7b-013666b6a9d0/npm-backend-1af7b017324abe646179a57d/lifecycle with those two hashed values in the "host" and "user" query parameters. No credentials, tokens, environment values, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted; the only filesystem access is /etc/hostname. The package declares no lifecycle scripts and has no other executable payload.
